title: h4reet.ai runtime
description: The stack's runtime: the kill switch, spend, requests, the model server, the audit log and alerts, telemetry health, the room's use (spec 002; §7.8), the cloud's hosts (spec 001; specs/001-cloud-elevation/contracts/tunnel.md §7), the studio's GPU windows (spec 003; specs/003-studio-assets/contracts/gpu-window.md §3), and dev-time usage on the Team plan, outside the production meter (spec 000; specs/000-local-foundations/contracts/telemetry.md §7). Provisioned from deploy/grafana/dashboards; edit the file, not the UI.

list.name: Studio GPU windows
list.textFormat: The model server is handed to a studio job: hello falls back within the sub-budget, or degrades (docs/runbooks/studio-gpu-window.md)

panels.title: Kill switch
panels.description: The stack's kill switch now: normal in green, degraded in red. An unreachable or empty store reads degraded, because an unknown state counts as degraded (FR-028, FR-031).

panels.title: Kill switch (state timeline)
panels.description: When the kill switch was normal and when degraded, in the dashboard's time range (FR-028, FR-033). Only a reset brings it back to normal.

panels.title: Why responses are degraded
panels.description: The cause a hello arriving now would get, in FR-022's order: none in green, any cause in red (FR-022, FR-028; contracts/gateway-http.md §3).

panels.title: Degraded responses by cause
panels.description: Which degraded causes answered, and when.

panels.title: Store state (authoritative)
panels.description: The kill switch, the renewal flag, and today's meters, straight from the store through grafana_ro, so it still answers when telemetry is down (data-model.md §2.9).

targets.rawSql: SELECT stack, env, state, since, crossed, fallback_awaiting_renewal, fallback_awaiting_since, day_key, month_key, day_spent_micro / 1e6 AS day_usd, month_spent_micro / 1e6 AS month_usd, fallback_spent_micro / 1e6 AS fallback_usd, fallback_allowance_micro / 1e6 AS fallback_allowance_usd, fallback_grant_no FROM gateway.v_state

panels.title: Paid adapters' months (authoritative)
panels.description: Each paid adapter's month as the store holds it, through grafana_ro and gateway.v_adapter_months, so it still reads when telemetry is down (spec 010, FR-036).

targets.rawSql: SELECT adapter, month, spent_micro / 1e6 AS spent_usd, reserved_micro / 1e6 AS reserved_usd, warned_at, reached_at FROM gateway.v_adapter_months ORDER BY month DESC, adapter

panels.title: Spend today
panels.description: Today's metered spend (UTC) against its warning and its ceiling, from the gateway's own meter (FR-028).

panels.title: Spend today (stat)
panels.description: Today's spend now, beside its warning and its ceiling.

panels.title: Spend month-to-date
panels.description: This month's metered spend (UTC) against its warning and its ceiling (FR-028).

panels.title: Spend month-to-date (stat)
panels.description: This month's spend now, beside its warning and its ceiling.

panels.title: Fallback sub-budget remaining
panels.description: What fallback can still spend today: the allowance minus committed fallback spend; whether it awaits the operator's renewal, in red; and the current grant's warning (FR-028, FR-030).

panels.title: Fallback sub-budget remaining (time series)
panels.description: Fallback's room through the day, with the renewal flag on the right axis.

panels.title: Cost by provider and attribution
panels.description: Committed cost in the dashboard's time range, by provider, model, and attribution: Bedrock's fallback and test cost beside local's zero (FR-023, SC-005). On prod, provider aws.bedrock is the paid fallback: attribution fallback is hello's fallback calls, and test the Author's live contract test and Bedrock evals (POST /admin/adapters/bedrock/complete). Provider local is always 0, attributed none; dev's synthetic spend shows as provider synthetic. In USD to the micro-dollar, as the meter keeps it.

panels.title: Paid adapter's month against its cap
panels.description: Each capped paid adapter's UTC month, the Anthropic API's when prod's route names it, against its warning and its cap (spec 010, FR-036). At the cap the adapter is refused, adapter_month_spent, and local answers go on.

panels.title: Paid adapter's month against its cap (stat)
panels.description: Each capped paid adapter's month now, beside its warning and its cap (spec 010).

panels.title: Request count
panels.description: Requests a second, by the route each took (FR-028).

panels.title: Request count over the range
panels.description: Every request in the dashboard's time range.

panels.title: Error rate
panels.description: The share of requests answered 502 local_error or an unexpected 5xx; degraded answers are by design and not counted. With no traffic it has no value (telemetry.md §7.3).

panels.title: Latency p50 and p95
panels.description: From a request's arrival to its answer (FR-028).

panels.title: Provider latency p95
panels.description: Each provider attempt, by provider.

panels.title: Outcomes
panels.description: Requests by outcome: ok, degraded, refused, invalid, error.

panels.title: Model-server health
panels.description: The model server answers its metrics once its model is loaded; and each adapter's health as the gateway sees it (FR-028): local, and on prod bedrock, the paid fallback. bedrock reads down while its credentials are missing, expired, or refused, or while its circuit is open after three failed calls (contracts/provider-adapter.md §2.4 and §6). Runbooks: docs/runbooks/model-server-down.md, docs/runbooks/bedrock-unavailable.md, and, before the SSO session ends, docs/runbooks/bedrock-credentials-expiring.md.

panels.title: Generation
panels.description: Tokens a second the model server generated, and read from prompts.

panels.title: Queue
panels.description: Requests the model server is working on, and those waiting for a slot.

panels.title: Tokens by provider
panels.description: Input and output tokens in the dashboard's time range, by provider.

panels.title: Audit log
panels.description: Every operator action and every automatic trip, with who, when, and why, straight from the store's append-only audit log through grafana_ro (FR-034). Filtered on the real time it was recorded, so dev's test-clock jumps stay in range; the gateway's own time is beside it.

targets.rawSql: SELECT recorded_at AS "time", ts AS gateway_time, actor, action, reason, before::text AS before, after::text AS after FROM gateway.audit_log WHERE $__timeFilter(recorded_at) ORDER BY recorded_at DESC LIMIT 200

panels.title: Alerts by channel and outcome
panels.description: Delivery attempts in the dashboard's time range, by channel, kind, outcome (delivered, retry, or failed; FR-032), and form: designed, plain, or none for a channel given up with no attempt (spec 011, FR-044). A failed channel is the runbook alert-channel-down.md.

panels.title: Alerts sent as plain text by fallback
panels.description: Attempts that sent the plain form in the designed one's place, in the dashboard's time range, by channel, kind, and reason: entities_refused, message_refused, render_failed, over_limit, or not_rendered (spec 011, FR-045, FR-046). The alert arrived in today's form; the runbook alert-channel-down.md says what each reason means.

panels.title: Alert delivery lag p95
panels.description: From an alert's commit to its delivery; FR-032 allows 5 minutes.

panels.title: Operator actions
panels.description: Accepted operator writes in the dashboard's time range, by action, and the dev-only test endpoints refused outside dev.

panels.title: Alert log
panels.description: The alert outbox's events from the gateway's log: queued, delivered, retry, failed, and fallback (spec 011: an attempt that sent the plain form in the designed one's place). Empty while telemetry is down; the store keeps the outbox (contracts/alerts.md §4.4).

panels.title: Audit events, from the logs
panels.description: The audit records the gateway logs (event.name h4.audit). The Audit log table above reads the store itself and outlasts a telemetry outage.

panels.title: Backends up
panels.description: Each scraped backend, one per job: how a degraded telemetry pipeline shows itself (plan §19).

panels.title: Spend freshness
panels.description: Seconds since the day's spend gauge was last seen: green under 30, amber under 60, red at 60 or more or with no data (telemetry.md §6.5 and §7.6).

panels.title: Export failures
panels.description: Spans, metric points, and log records an exporter failed to send, a second.

panels.title: Dropped at the queue
panels.description: Telemetry an exporter's full queue dropped, a second.

panels.title: Queue fill
panels.description: How full each exporter's sending queue is.

panels.title: Spans to Langfuse
panels.description: Spans the collector sent to Langfuse, a second.

panels.title: Refused at the receiver
panels.description: Telemetry the collector's receivers refused, a second: its memory limit, or a malformed request.

panels.title: Use per object per day
panels.description: Each object's selections, by pointer, touch, or the list, in the 24 hours before the range's end, from the room's usage events (spec 002, FR-054, FR-056). An event carries its kind and the ID alone, so nothing here says who selected it. For a past day, end the range at that day's midnight; the dashboard is in UTC.

panels.title: Use per item per day
panels.description: Each resume item's selections in the 24 hours before the range's end, from the room's usage events (spec 002, FR-054, FR-056); only the IDs config/room-events.yaml lists are counted. An event carries its kind and the ID alone, so nothing here says who selected it. For a past day, end the range at that day's midnight; the dashboard is in UTC.

panels.title: PDF downloads per day
panels.description: The resume's PDF link followed, on any screen, in the 24 hours before each moment; the number is the last, at the range's end (spec 002, FR-056). For a past day, end the range at that day's midnight; the dashboard is in UTC.

panels.title: Visits shown the 2D mode
panels.description: The share of visits the room showed in its 2D mode (the visitor's choice, a slow device, a lost context, or no WebGL 2) over the dashboard's range: mode_2d events over resume_kept, a stand-in for visits, which the room sends once a visit at the hand-off's end (spec 033, FR-003), since no visit is counted (spec 002, FR-054, FR-056). A range that reaches back before the release that carries spec 033 to the serving host (a range between the merge and that release too) leaves out of the denominator the visits then that read the resume at once, which sent resume_opened instead, so the share reads high for that span; with no visit in the range it has no value.

panels.title: Visits whose avatar failed
panels.description: The share of visits in which a figure's avatar file failed to load after its retry, so the figure showed its fallback (spec 009, FR-032, FR-034): the twin's own model or one of its clips among them since spec 016 (its FR-050, FR-051), the twin then showing the stand-in, the room's dog's model or one of its clips since spec 025 (its FR-026), in dinosaur visits since spec 028 (its FR-018), the dog then not showing, and the visitors' avatars' files: avatar_failed events, at most one a visit and with no identifier, over resume_kept, a stand-in for visits, which the room sends once a visit at the hand-off's end (spec 033, FR-003), read as the 2D share is read. A range that reaches back before the release that carries spec 033 to the serving host (a range between the merge and that release too) leaves out of the denominator the visits then that read the resume at once, which sent resume_opened instead, so the share reads high for that span; with no visit in the range it has no value.

panels.title: Turns sent and talk presses
panels.description: The text box's sends and the talk button's presses, and when (spec 002, FR-054). Until the twin's conversation exists, each answers with a fixed message and calls nothing; its cost, latency, and turns per room feature come with conversations (telemetry.md §7.8).

panels.title: Events refused
panels.description: Usage events the gateway refused, by reason: content_type (415, neither JSON nor text), shape (400, not {kind} or {kind, id}), kind (400, a kind config/room-events.yaml doesn't list), and id (400, an ID it doesn't list for the kind; every event while the file is missing or invalid, which the gateway's startup log names as room_events.unavailable). The room never retries one, so the use panels undercount by these (spec 002, contracts/room-events.md §3).

panels.title: Visits that walked
panels.description: The share of visits that entered the walking view over the dashboard's range: walk_started events, one a visit at its first entry, over resume_kept, a stand-in for visits, which the room sends once a visit at the hand-off's end (spec 033, FR-003), since no visit is counted (spec 008, FR-051, FR-053; spec 002, FR-054). A range that reaches back before the release that carries spec 033 to the serving host (a range between the merge and that release too) leaves out of the denominator the visits then that read the resume at once, which sent resume_opened instead, so the share reads high for that span; with no visit in the range it has no value.

panels.title: Visits in full screen
panels.description: The share of visits that entered full screen over the dashboard's range: fullscreen_entered events, one a visit at its first entry, over resume_kept, a stand-in for visits, which the room sends once a visit at the hand-off's end (spec 033, FR-003), since no visit is counted (spec 005, FR-060, FR-062; spec 002, FR-054). A range that reaches back before the release that carries spec 033 to the serving host (a range between the merge and that release too) leaves out of the denominator the visits then that read the resume at once, which sent resume_opened instead, so the share reads high for that span; with no visit in the range it has no value. A browser that offers no full screen, as an iPhone's, shows no control, so its visits never count here.

panels.title: Visits whose loading was cut short
panels.description: The share of visits whose loading screen gave way at its 7-second ceiling with the room's files still loading, over the dashboard's range: loading_cut_short events, one a visit, over resume_kept, a stand-in for visits, which the room sends once a visit at the hand-off's end (spec 033, FR-003), since no visit is counted (spec 012, FR-046, FR-048; spec 002, FR-054). It shows how often the ceiling binds, which says whether the first visit is too heavy for visitors' connections. A rough share, in both directions: 2D visits count in the denominator and never show the loader, which pulls it low; and the event is sent before the hand-off, so a visit cut short that leaves before the hand-off's end counts in the numerator alone, which pulls it high; and a range that reaches back before the release that carries spec 033 to the serving host (a range between the merge and that release too) leaves out of the denominator the visits then that read the resume at once, which sent resume_opened instead, so the share reads high for that span. With no visit in the range it has no value.

panels.title: Turns per feature, by outcome
panels.description: The twin's turns on POST /room/turn, by the piece that opened the conversation (or free_talk) and how each ended: ok, withheld (a guard replaced the answer), degraded, refused (a limit), not_ready, invalid, or error (spec 007, FR-044, FR-045). No visitor data: the feature is a selectable's ID from the twin's pack.

panels.title: Cost per feature, today
panels.description: Each feature's spend over the 24 hours before the range's end, beside its latency and errors (Principle V): the meter's committed cost of the twin's calls, from h4_cost_usd_total by h4_room_feature. Local answers cost $0; the Author's evaluation calls, attributed test, are left out (spec 007, FR-045).

panels.title: Turn latency, p95 by feature
panels.description: Each feature's 95th-percentile time from a turn's arrival to its response, the whole answer after the guards (spec 007, FR-044, FR-045; SC-003 reads it on prod's local model).

panels.title: Cost per feature, 30 days
panels.description: Each feature's spend over the 30 days before the range's end, a rolling window (the meter's own month stays the calendar's); evaluation calls left out (spec 007, FR-045).

panels.title: Turn errors by feature
panels.description: Turns that ended in error or degraded, by feature (spec 007, FR-045): the causes are in the next panel.

panels.title: Degraded turns by cause
panels.description: Degraded turns by spec 000's cause, or twin_unavailable when the twin's files or prod's limits.twin are missing (spec 007, FR-045, FR-054). The room shows each cause's fixed message.

panels.title: Answers withheld, by guard
panels.description: Answers the guards withheld or replaced before they left the gateway, by guard: numbers, amounts, disclosure (in a turn that asks who or what the twin is, replaced by the profile's disclosure line), prompt, secrets, links, ownership, seva, location, surname, address, privacy, agents_share, restated_claim, repair_opener (an answer delivered without its opening agreement, or withheld when agreement was all it said: the turn's outcome, ok or withheld, tells them apart), length, or error (spec 007, FR-021, FR-044; seva since its plan's D28, location and surname since D29). Beside them, query B: the answers delivered with a sentence removed, by each guard that removed one (numbers, amounts in a cost question, seva, address, restated_claim), with "email address" made "email" (address_repair), or with the corpus's claim tags taken off (claim_tags), each answer counted once for each (D40, D41); address and restated_claim show in query A only when too little was left to deliver. Each still cost its call.

panels.title: Answered locally
panels.description: The share of answered turns the local model answered over the dashboard's range, the rest by the capped fallback (spec 007, FR-045; SC-010 expects all of them while the local tier is healthy). A degraded or refused turn counts in neither part; with no answered turn it has no value.

panels.title: The model each turn used
panels.description: The model each of the twin's calls asked for over the last day, by feature, straight from the store through grafana_ro (gateway.v_twin_models: no client label, request ID, or trace ID), so it still answers when telemetry is down (spec 007, FR-045; departure D7).

targets.rawSql: SELECT request_model, room_feature, count(*) AS turns FROM gateway.v_twin_models WHERE ts > now() - interval '1 day' GROUP BY request_model, room_feature ORDER BY turns DESC

panels.title: Tunnel up
panels.description: Each end of the laptop's tunnel: the laptop's connection, and the tunnel end's three reverse forwards (spec 001 FR-060; contracts/tunnel.md §7).

panels.title: Tunnel up (state timeline)
panels.description: When each end of the tunnel was up and down, in the dashboard's time range (spec 001 FR-060).

panels.title: Tunnel reconnects
panels.description: New connections after the first, per hour, on each end: a flapping tunnel shows here before visitors see it.

panels.title: Telemetry delayed at the tunnel end
panels.description: How full the tunnel end's collector's file-backed queue is, per host it sends to: a host that's gone fills its queue, and the queue empties when it's back.

panels.title: Telemetry lost at the tunnel end
panels.description: What the tunnel end's collector's full queue refused, per host it sends to: spans, metric points, and log records lost.

panels.title: Shared state latency, p95
panels.description: The 95th percentile of each host's queries and sessions on prod's shared state, the tunnel end's Postgres (spec 001 FR-060; contracts/shared-state.md §10).

panels.title: Shared state errors
panels.description: Each host's failures on the shared state, by the error's class, never its message: a host that can't read it answers degraded (spec 001 FR-019, FR-060).

panels.title: Last good backup's age
panels.description: Seconds since the tunnel end's last good hourly dump reached its bucket: green under 2 hours, red from 2 hours and on no data (spec 001 FR-019; contracts/shared-state.md §10).

panels.title: The release on each host
panels.description: The release each cloud host's deployer runs, its commit, and who started it: deployer, or the Author by hand (spec 001 FR-049; contracts/releases-deployer.md §6). Never an address, an account, or a digest.

panels.title: Deployments
panels.description: Each deployer's attempts by host and outcome: deployed, refused, rolled back, or a rollback that failed (spec 001 FR-046, FR-047; contracts/releases-deployer.md §6).

panels.title: Which host serves
panels.description: The host the relay on the tunnel end sends visitors to: the laptop while it is healthy, else EC2, else none, in red (spec 001 FR-054, FR-060; contracts/relay-http.md §4, §9).

panels.title: Handovers and their gaps
panels.description: Each change of serving host the relay recorded, its reason, and the time no host served on a move out of none, straight from the shared state through grafana_ro (gateway.v_handovers: no address or client), so it still answers when telemetry is down (spec 001 SC-007, SC-016; data-model.md §1.2).

targets.rawSql: SELECT at AS "time", from_host, to_host, reason, gap_ms / 1000.0 AS gap_s FROM gateway.v_handovers ORDER BY at DESC LIMIT 50

panels.title: The relay's requests by host and outcome
panels.description: The relay's requests a second, by the host it sent each to (or none) and how each ended: answered, degraded, refused, or a status request; never by address (spec 001 FR-060; contracts/relay-http.md §9).

panels.title: The public cap's refusals
panels.description: Requests the relay's public cap refused in each hour, by its limit: per minute, per day, or in flight across every address; never by address (spec 001 FR-033; ADR 0029).

panels.title: EC2's state
panels.description: EC2's state, from the sink's read every 2 minutes; no data while the read fails (spec 001 FR-060; contracts/handover.md §10).

panels.title: EC2's spot request
panels.description: Its persistent spot request's state: `disabled` while AWS holds it after an interruption (FR-071) (spec 001 FR-060; contracts/handover.md §10).

panels.title: EC2's starts, refusals, and the guard's stops
panels.description: The start function's and the guard's outcomes in the last hour, by trigger and outcome, outside_hours' refusals among them (FR-065, FR-071) (spec 001 FR-060; contracts/handover.md §10).

panels.title: The hours' scheduled starts and stops
panels.description: Each scheduled open and close of EC2's hours, by its outcome: recorded, and alerted only when it needs the Author (ADR 0048) (spec 001 FR-060; contracts/handover.md §10).

panels.title: The autostart switch
panels.description: on lets EC2 start automatically; off stops that (contracts/handover.md §5) (spec 001 FR-060; contracts/handover.md §10).

panels.title: The laptop's health check
panels.description: The share of Route 53's checkers that see the laptop's health block answer through the tunnel end (FR-054) (spec 001 FR-060; contracts/handover.md §10).

panels.title: The handover window
panels.description: The last takeover's window, from the relay's first laptop to EC2's stop: green under 300 s, red from 300 s (FR-063) (spec 001 FR-060; contracts/handover.md §10).

panels.title: The server's month against its budget
panels.description: h4-server-month's month to date against its figure, read once an hour, beside model spend above (FR-021; User Story 7) (spec 001 FR-060; contracts/handover.md §10).

panels.title: The public view's age
panels.description: The public view's host part's age at the sink's last write: green under 300 s, red from 300 s (FR-058) (spec 001 FR-060; contracts/public-view.md §5).

panels.title: The public view's writes and posts
panels.description: The sink's writes of site/status/latest.json by outcome, and each host's posts to it by outcome, over the last hour (FR-057) (spec 001 FR-060; contracts/public-view.md §5).

panels.title: Host types
panels.description: The listed type each host runs, from its Name tag: a change is a replace onto another type when one had no spot capacity (spec 032 FR-018; contracts/handover.md §10).

panels.title: Fallback spend in studio windows
panels.description: Each studio GPU window in the dashboard's time range, from its start to its end (blank while it is open), with the ledger's fallback spend and calls between them, straight from the store through grafana_ro (gateway.v_studio_windows), so it still answers when telemetry is down. A window hands the model server's GPU to a studio job: hello falls back within the sub-budget, or degrades, and no budget or ceiling changes for it (spec 003 FR-035, SC-011). The time series' shaded regions are the same windows, from h4_studio_window. Runbook: docs/runbooks/studio-gpu-window.md.

targets.rawSql: SELECT started_at AS "time", ended_at, fallback_micro / 1e6 AS fallback_usd, fallback_calls FROM gateway.v_studio_windows WHERE started_at <= $__timeTo() AND (ended_at IS NULL OR ended_at >= $__timeFrom()) ORDER BY started_at DESC LIMIT 50

panels.title: Development time on the Team plan: notional cost, outside the production meter
Claude Code notional cost by model
panels.description: Claude Code's own accounting of its sessions in the dashboard's time range, by model: notional cost on the Team plan's flat fee, outside the production meter (FR-037): it never adds to h4_cost_usd_total or the ceilings. Only prod's collector receives it (edge's x004), so dev and dev-cpu show none. For a month's figure, set the range to the month; Prometheus keeps 30 days.

panels.title: Claude Code notional cost by model (stat)
panels.description: The same sums as the table, one tile per model: notional cost on the Team plan's flat fee, outside the production meter (FR-037): it never adds to h4_cost_usd_total or the ceilings. Only prod's collector receives it (edge's x004), so dev and dev-cpu show none.

panels.title: Claude Code tokens by type
panels.description: Claude Code's tokens in the dashboard's time range, by type: input, output, cacheRead, and cacheCreation. They carry the notional cost on the Team plan's flat fee, outside the production meter (FR-037): it never adds to h4_cost_usd_total or the ceilings. Only prod's collector receives it (edge's x004), so dev and dev-cpu show none.

panels.title: Agent-config eval runs: notional cost
panels.description: The behavioral agent-config evals' cost in the dashboard's time range: each run the Author's gate recorded from evals/agent-config/history/ (plan §14; telemetry.md §4.4), counted once however often it was posted. It is notional cost on the Team plan's flat fee, outside the production meter (FR-037): it never adds to h4_cost_usd_total or the ceilings. Only prod's collector receives it (edge's x004), so dev and dev-cpu show none.

panels.title: Agent-config eval runs: tokens
panels.description: The behavioral agent-config evals' tokens in the dashboard's time range, by type: input, output, cache_read, and cache_creation, from each recorded run's history entry. They carry the notional cost on the Team plan's flat fee, outside the production meter (FR-037): it never adds to h4_cost_usd_total or the ceilings. Only prod's collector receives it (edge's x004), so dev and dev-cpu show none.

panels.title: Agent-config eval runs
panels.description: Each behavioral agent-config eval run the gate recorded in the dashboard's time range: its history entry in evals/agent-config/history/ (<UTC>-<branch>-<sha>), its verdict, and its cost, notional cost on the Team plan's flat fee, outside the production meter (FR-037): it never adds to h4_cost_usd_total or the ceilings. Only prod's collector receives it (edge's x004), so dev and dev-cpu show none. The committed history is the long-term record (SC-008).
